head: MERGEABLE — 0 blocker, 2 should, 6 note. The frozen law holds against the LIVE origin/main (7e40e3be, re-fetched at review end, unmoved): check-frozen-workflows.mjs exits 0 (296 files, 53 "use workflow" modules, 3 retired), --compare-base origin/main reports 278 entries unchanged in hash AND deployed flag, 18 additions, 0 removals, main's `retired` block is byte-identical (591-byte tail, three chatTurn entries, #810), none of the three retired FILES is in the tree, workflowBodies is 53 with chatTurn_v1 absent and chatTurn_v2..v20 / claraWork_v1..v4 / clientOnboarding_v1..v5 all still exported, and check (d) monotonicity passes against origin/main (v19→v20, v3→v4, v4→v5, no class removed). My independent closure walk over the three new roots reproduces 86 members, 0 missing from the manifest, 0 first-party escapes, 0 members outside packages/, and the one module-level `node:` import is the inherited interview.v1.steps.ts:11 (F11, unchanged). parts-parity, the bundle gate and worker-paths are green; typecheck, the nitro build and lint are exit 0; every DB call site in the three closures matches the live 0224 signatures (7-arg admit_staff_expense_claim_work, 12-arg create_accrual_adjustment_for, 5-arg complete_fixed_asset_particulars_for). I raced F1–F7 individually and all seven are closed: F1 at the live door (a door-shaped answer with a string driver, a blank optional and a reserved note ACCEPTS; the number spelling REFUSES CLR10 constraint 'text') AND in a real World — fixed-asset-acquisition-e2e leg 2b now drives the particulars question positively end to end; F2 interview-kill-resume-e2e PASS; F3 all 18 notes filled with the NEW numbers (0216/0219/0221/0222/0192) and --update preserves notes by code; F4 {kind:'fixed_asset',asset_id} accepted by the door with an open read-side type; F5 client-over-firm proven on four packs; F6 the de-duplicated option list ACCEPTS where the duplicated one REFUSES option_values_unique, and both opens are wrapped; F7 the provenance item satisfies ck_onboarding_plan_items_answer and moves no commit gate. two-build-cutover-e2e is ALL PASS with the retired-v1 roster (A 52 / B 53), rollback REFUSED naming claraWork_v4, scoped-allow granted, chat half resumed on v19 inside B. Nothing cites an old wave number: zero hits for the eleven old stems, and the five added lines carrying a bare 0203 all name main's 0203_list_accounting_work_intent_key. The two `should`s are a precedence hole F5's fix did not cover (the interview fold prefers a governed record over the legacy row the pack itself flags `authoritative`, for entity_type/msic — both keys live in BOTH registers on the merged chain) and two F3 manifest notes that assert a web import which cannot exist. --lock-deployed has correctly not run, so both are still cheap.

findings.what: F5 made client-over-firm explicit but left the precedence that actually decides two of the six mapped keys. clara.get_knowledge_pack appends the LEGACY clara.client_facts rows AFTER the governed ones and flags each `authoritative: true` — "the value the ESTATE acts on is still the legacy one" (0192's own words). The fold reads knowledge_key, value, record_id, knowledge_version, trust, source_kind and scope_kind, and never `authoritative`; both rows are scope_kind:'client', so the FIRST one wins and that is the governed, non-authoritative one. The interview then SKIPS the question with a value the rest of the estate does not act on. The cut's own sibling module already gets this right — recordLine marks `source_kind === 'legacy_client_fact' || authoritative === true` as "in force" for the Work lane — so two lanes in one cut disagree about which recorded fact governs.
findings.evidence: Measured on the live 0224 chain (clara_int3 @55621): `select knowledge_key from clara.knowledge_keys` and `select fact_key from clara.client_fact_keys` OVERLAP on exactly entity_type and msic, and both are in KNOWN_FACT_KEYS (interview.v4.known.ts:75-82). The order is structural: 0192_client_knowledge_records.sql:1502 aggregates the governed rows `order by knowledge_key`, then :1524 does `v_rows := v_rows || clara._knowledge_legacy_rows(...)`; the legacy builder (0192:1051-1078) emits 'scope_kind','client' and 'authoritative', true on every row. Driven through the real fold: a pack of [governed entity_type=sdn_bhd, legacy entity_type=llp(authoritative)] returns {value:'sdn_bhd', recordId:'r-governed'} — the non-authoritative one. Wall 1 does not catch it: both values are canonical ENTITY_TYPES_V2 members, so the segment validator accepts either. The docblock at :112-128 reasons only about the client/firm pair and never mentions the legacy union, while the module header at :36-40 enumerates the OTHER three legacy keys (trade_nature, banking_arrangement, customer_identity_policy) as "no segment at all" — so the legacy set was in view when these two were not.
findings.fix: In the fold, prefer a row with `authoritative === true` (equivalently source_kind === 'legacy_client_fact') over a governed row under the same key, above the existing client-over-firm rule — one more comparison beside the two already there — or drop entity_type and msic from KNOWN_FACT_KEYS until the legacy register is retired. Correct the docblock either way, and add the cell the F5 round already has the shape for: a pack of [governed, legacy] under entity_type must fold to the legacy row. No migration and no door change, so it is still a --update away.

findings.what: Two of F3's eighteen new notes — the record the --lock-deployed ceremony and every later reader consult — state a provenance fact that is false. Both say the browser imports the frozen module: "(the web question form imports the same module and is NOT frozen — only this closure membership locks it)" and "(the web form imports the same module ...)". apps/web cannot import @clara/runtime at all. The clause was copied from #643's existing note on lib/periodic-adjustment-basis.ts (:68), which carries the same error, so F3 propagated it rather than inventing it — but these two entries are this round's, and the note exists precisely to tell the next hand what else moves when this file moves. It points at a consumer that does not exist and away from the real ones: apps/web keeps hand-maintained MIRRORS that nothing in the freeze closure locks.
findings.evidence: apps/web/lib/checkout/stripe-session.test.ts:445 states it outright: "apps/web cannot import @clara/runtime (it is not a dependency; this app builds for Cloudflare)". apps/web/lib/registers/fa-refusal-field.ts:9-14 is the mirror and says why: "WHY A SECOND COPY OF THE MAP. packages/runtime/lib/fixed-asset-acquisition.ts carries the same axis→field table ... apps/web does not depend on @clara/runtime (nothing under apps/web imports it, and the package is not in apps/web's dependencies), so this is a deliberate MIRROR rather than an import". Greps confirm: apps/web contains no import of packages/runtime/lib/fixed-asset-acquisition or .../accrual-basis (prose citations only), and apps/web/package.json lists no @clara/* dependency. The DEPLOY ORDER half of both notes is correct and independently verified (0222 defines clara.create_accrual_adjustment_for, 0216 defines clara.complete_fixed_asset_particulars_for — the only definitions of either name under packages/db/migrations).
findings.fix: Replace the clause in both notes with what is true and useful — apps/web carries a hand-maintained MIRROR (lib/registers/fa-refusal-field.ts, pinned by fa-refusal-field.test.ts; the accrual form's own copy) that this hash lock does NOT cover, so a change here needs the mirror moved in the same commit — then re-run --update (it preserves prev.note, scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs:264, so this is a hand edit plus a no-op re-run). Worth correcting #643's copy at :68 in the same pass, since that is where the sentence came from.

findings.what: The fix round credits a gate with a property it does not have: "check-dead-citations (which is what proves every 0180:… / 0017:… citation added above resolves)". That script is a dead-NAME guard for three specific doc names; it never opens a migration and never resolves a line number. So the round's line-number citations — the load-bearing evidence for F1, F5, F6 and F7 — are backed by no gate, which matters because the next reader will trust the gate instead of re-checking.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-dead-citations.mjs:3-25: "the repo-wide DEAD-NAME GUARD for #755 and #690 ... a comment cites a doc that does not exist anywhere in this repository"; its success line is "clean — no citation of apps/web/AGENTS.md, db-tests.md or ARCHITECTURE Appendix A anywhere in the repository". I hand-checked six of the round's citations instead and all six resolve exactly: 0180:477-482 is the `else -- text` arm raising constraint 'text'; 0180:847 is `set status='answered', answer = p_answer`; 0180:394-398 is option_values_unique; 0017:1045-1046 is the item_kind/item_key CHECK pair; 0017:2492 is `create function clara.begin_client_onboarding`; 0017:2680-2681 is the `case when v_state='pending' then null else p_answered_by end` stamp; 0192:1502 is the `jsonb_agg(j order by knowledge_key)`. The citations are sound; only the claim about the gate is wrong.
findings.fix: Restate the row as what lint actually runs (freeze-lint plus its three selftests, check-dead-citations for the three dead doc names, 13 sibling checkers, eslint) and say the migration line citations were spot-checked by hand. If a resolving gate is wanted, it is a new checker, not this one.

findings.what: F7(a)'s stated motive — "a firm that filled part of the plan from the dashboard and THEN started the interview was asked every one of those questions again by v4" — names a path that does not exist today, and both the file comment and the report state it as a present fact rather than as a guard for a surface that has not shipped. The code is correct and safe (it folds {} on every reachable path, which is why both World interview legs are unmoved); the claim around it is the problem, under the same evidence rule the round invokes elsewhere.
findings.evidence: Three independent walls, each measured. (1) No writer: clara.update_onboarding_plan is called only from packages/runtime/src/interviewRoutes.ts and the clientOnboarding bodies — a grep over apps/web finds only /rest/v1/rpc/begin_client_onboarding, and clara.begin_client_onboarding (0017:2492) seeds no items, as the round itself measured. (2) No second run: a plan already bound by an `interview_run` item self-terminates superseded_by_existing_run at clientOnboarding.v5.ts:131-135 BEFORE the fold is reached, so a later run cannot see an earlier run's answered items. (3) No same-run replay: plan0 comes from a memoised step, so a WDK resume replays the original (empty) item list — which is exactly why interview-kill-resume-e2e still answers 16 and writes 17 (measured PASS on a pristine copy, this review).
findings.fix: Re-word the comment and the report line to "the surface that will write those items does not exist yet; this is the guard for it", or name the ticket that adds the dashboard writer. No code change.

findings.what: F6's two wrappers assume a throw means the door did nothing. If clara.open_work_question COMMITS and the step's result is then lost (the connection drops after commit and the WDK's retries are exhausted), `.catch(() => null)` runs with a pending question row and a bound hook token already durable: the model branch settles failed/internal saying "nobody was asked", and the particulars branch settles completed with question_not_opened saying "nobody was asked" — while a live question sits on a task that is now terminal and whose hook nothing will ever resume. The wrapping is still right (it replaced a sentence that falsely denied a posted entry); it is the two new sentences that can be false in this one window.
findings.evidence: Both call sites end `.catch(() => null)` and branch on `opened === null`. The payload texts are claraWork.v4.errors.ts:91-93 ("could not be opened, so nobody was asked") and :120-123 ("nothing was posted and nobody was asked. Re-running the Work is safe"). The door is idempotent on the hook token (claraWork.v4.ts:45-46), which is what makes a WDK retry safe and what bounds this to the post-retry case. Neither branch is driven by any test — the round names that as its residual 2 — so this is read, not measured.
findings.fix: Cheapest honest version: in the catch, re-read clara.get_work_question for the task and pick the sentence from what is actually there (asked-but-unrecoverable vs never-asked). Otherwise add one clause to both payloads naming the window, so the next operator reading the Work does not conclude the question cannot exist.

findings.what: The integration worktree's only dirt is an un-ignored artifact directory left by the re-base runtime leg. `git status --porcelain` on a branch about to become a PR reports `?? e2e-run/`, so a `git add -A` at commit or clock-out time sweeps its TSVs, .done markers, poll.sh and two log directories into the wave's history.
findings.evidence: git status --porcelain → `?? e2e-run/` (the only entry, before and after all of this review's runs). Contents: ALL.done, ISO.done, SUMMARY.tsv, SUMMARY-iso.tsv, poll.sh, logs/, logs-iso/, timestamped 17:29–19:06 on 2026-09-17, i.e. the runtime-leg worker's. `git check-ignore -v` confirms the siblings ARE covered — .gitignore:65 `.scratch/` and .gitignore:13 `.output/` — so the two-build drill's scratch images and the nitro bundle are invisible and only this one is not.
findings.fix: Delete e2e-run/ before the PR, or add it beside `.scratch/` in .gitignore if the harness is meant to keep writing there.

findings.what: Recorded so the next runner does not read it as a regression: this leg cannot survive being run out of the action's order. Run fourth on a clara_wave_b_ci that three earlier legs had already used, it dies at ~84s with "FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory" (exit 134) while the in-process world's reconciler emits its render/sandbox UNWIRED lines in a tight loop — a failure that names nothing about the interview. CI is unaffected (action.yml runs it FIRST, on the pristine database), and the branch is not implicated.
findings.evidence: My chain: legs 1-3 (interview-kill-resume PASS 56s, fixed-asset-acquisition PASS 14s, chat-turn-v20 PASS 8s) then interview-e2e → exit 134 at 84s, V8 at the 4GB limit ("Mark-Compact 4017.7 (4143.9) -> 4012.0 MB ... allocation failure"). Re-run ISOLATED on a database freshly re-created `template clara_master` (pristine post-bootstrap: 2 firms, 0 tasks, 0 Work): INTERVIEW E2E: ALL PASS, exit 0, 84s — the two cancel scenarios, the full 16-segment drive to interview_complete with 17 items, and p649.interview.sst_park_closed. Same file, same image, same rig; only the database state differs. This matches DECISIONS §3.3(6) and the fix round's own §5 note about an unreproduced interview-e2e red.
findings.fix: None owed by this cut. If it is worth hardening: the leg runs the WDK world IN-PROCESS, so one line in its header saying it must run first on the pristine database (as action.yml already does), or a bound on the reconciler's log retention, turns a 4GB OOM into a readable skip.
